scope: Operational data flow only; no cryptographic security acceptance is granted.

evidence.supports: The baseline generation and local t8n reproduction are local workflows; the retained t8n route does not contact RPC or read .env.
The generator invokes a local native prover with local input/output paths and retains synthetic witness/proof artifacts.
All analyzed witnesses are explicitly synthetic benchmark material; the records do not document a production service, RPC, telemetry, path provider, isolation boundary, or attestation.

dataFlowFindings.finding: The research prover reads local witness files. This is not evidence for a remote witness service. A cross-user aggregator must never receive witnesses.
No remote proving execution or remote-memory protocol is retained. Do not infer confidentiality, availability, or performance for one.
No telemetry inventory, packet capture, opt-in state, redaction test, or disablement proof is retained. A production CLI must default to no telemetry.

The local baseline command does not need RPC, but no production root/history lookup is implemented. Querying a public RPC for a particular commitment, leaf index, root, or path can link network identity and timing to withdrawal interest.

Synthetic paths are local fixtures. No centralized production path provider is evaluated. A provider can learn commitment interest even without the secret and can deny, equivocate, or fingerprint responses.
Raw proof and ABI calldata bytes are measured. There is no retained upload transport, destination, timing, retry, proxy, or metadata-leakage test.
The pinned research binary proves locally, but no supported, packaged, portable production fallback exists and H2/H3 are unmeasured.

serviceAcceptanceRequirements.witnessPolicy: A cross-user aggregation service receives proofs and public statements only, never witnesses. A separately proposed single-user witness service would require explicit user consent and all controls below; it is not accepted by this review.
secureWitnessIsolation: Document the precise trust boundary, process/container/VM/TEE isolation mechanism, host administrator capability, memory lifetime, swap/core-dump policy, and destruction evidence.
Encrypt witness material in transit and at rest with per-job keys; do not log request bodies, filesystem paths, commitment interests, or derived secrets.
Prevent cross-tenant filesystem, cache, IPC, scheduler, and accelerator-memory reuse leaks; retain adversarial isolation tests.
Bind returned proof and public statement to the user's request and verify locally before submission.
Define incident response, retention, backup, subpoena/operator access, and deletion semantics.
attestationAssumptions: Pin measured code, parameters, CLI policy, and isolation configuration to reviewable digests.
Specify hardware/firmware vendor roots, verifier freshness, revocation, rollback resistance, debug state, and who operates the attestation verifier.
Treat attestation as evidence of measured software state, not proof that hardware, firmware, side channels, host I/O, or operator policy is trustworthy.
Provide an explicit non-attested local fallback; attestation failure must not silently downgrade.
telemetryPolicy: Disabled by default and provably absent from proof generation.
Never collect witness-derived data, note identifiers, commitment/path/root interests, addresses, RPC URLs, proof bytes, filenames, stable device identifiers, or fine-grained progress timing.
Any opt-in event schema, endpoint, retention period, and deletion procedure must be published and packet-capture tested.
rpcAndPathPolicy: Support user-selected RPC and locally synchronized history; do not silently contact a default provider.
Prefer batch/range history acquisition that does not single out one commitment and verify roots/paths locally.
Authenticate source and chain/fork identity, detect equivocation, and permit multiple providers or a local node.
Do not send a private witness or nullifier secret to an RPC or path provider.
localFallback: Same proof system and statement as the service path, with no service-only transcript or format.
Offline proving after explicit user-supplied public history/path input.
Supported on measured H2 hardware with documented resource checks and no >8 GiB claim unless measured.
Locally verify proof and public-statement binding before any upload.

residualRisks: A proof or public statement may still reveal transaction intent and timing when uploaded or submitted.
An RPC/path provider may correlate broad history requests by network metadata even when no witness is sent.
Local proving may leak via OS telemetry, swap, crash dumps, other users, malware, or backups; none was tested.
Fresh hiding randomness in the baseline prevents byte-identical proof comparison and is not a crash-recovery design.
No service isolation, attestation, deployed RPC/path workflow, packet capture, or production fallback has been evaluated.
gateEffect: No privacy item repairs the mandatory absence of H2/H3 measurements or a practical CLI; SP-73 remains FAIL.
